# MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 - Calibration checks - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Scope
This procedure defines the calibration check activity for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 control and monitoring instrumentation, focusing on dust collector differential monitoring, media feed detection, and lubrication confirmation for moving components. The objective is to verify that detection thresholds, alarms, and status indicators are functioning and that maintenance records capture the results required for traceability. This procedure is supplemental to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05 and assumes operators have reviewed those documents prior to performing this activity.

Tools
- Calibrated differential pressure gauge compatible with the dust collector tap.  
- Portable signal simulator for discrete and analog inputs.  
- Inspected inspection mirror and flashlight for visual checks.  
- Clean rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P3-L1-04.  
- Lubricant stock labeled CFW-LUB-278 and tools for application.  
- Equipment logbook or electronic maintenance record access per SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by site PPE standards referenced in SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Routine calibration checks confirm that sensors and alarms reflect actual process conditions. The dust collector differential monitoring is critical for maintaining capture efficiency; an incorrect reading may mask filter loading or bypass conditions. Verifying the media feed detection ensures shot delivery consistency. Confirming proper lubricant presence and application protects mechanical drive components and reduces wear that can lead to off-spec parts.

Preparatory actions
Verify lockout and tagout per SOP-P3-L1-02 before opening access panels or performing any work that exposes moving parts. Confirm that the equipment is in a safe state and that blast media is retained or isolated to prevent inadvertent release. Review previous calibration entries in the equipment log to identify recurring trends.

Calibration check sequence
- Visual inspection: With access panels secured per safety requirements, inspect housings, ductwork, and sensor mounts for damage, blockage, or loose wiring. Clean sightlines for the dust collector tap using approved solvent and rags if deposits are present. Note any physical anomalies in the logbook and attach photographs where helpful for future review.

- Dust collector differential verification: Connect the calibrated differential pressure gauge to the dust collector tap. Compare the gauge reading to the cabinet’s differential pressure transducer output using the portable signal simulator or the instrument display. Confirm that the system will trigger at the documented alarm threshold and that the alarm annunciation is functional. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Document the gauge reading and the corresponding transducer output in the maintenance record. If the transducer output does not correspond to the gauge reading within expected operational tolerance, flag for corrective action and reference SOP-P3-L1-04 for instrument repair workflow.

- Media feed detector check: Use the signal simulator to reproduce an absence and a presence condition at the detector input. Observe PLC ladder status and local indicator lamps for correct transition and interlock behavior. Record simulated input values and the cabinet response. If detector response is inconsistent, perform connector and wiring continuity checks and reference SOP-P3-L1-05 for sensor replacement parts and procurement.

- Lubrication confirmation: Verify that the moving components identified in the preventive maintenance plan are free-moving and that lubricant is present. Confirm that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is CFW-LUB-278 and that the batch label on the lubricant used matches site inventory records. Apply lubricants sparingly to specified points, working to a clean finish, and wipe any excess. Note any unusual friction or play and escalate for mechanical inspection if present.

- Alarm and HMI validation: Simulate alarm conditions where permitted and verify that the cabinet HMI and central monitoring receive and display correct alarm text and severity. Confirm that acknowledgement and reset function as per operator interface design in SOP-P3-L1-02. Log any discrepancies and attach HMI screenshots when available.

Examples and expected outcomes
A typical acceptable outcome for the differential verification will show the calibrated gauge reading aligned with the transducer output and alarm annunciation at the configured setpoint. An example record entry would include the gauge model, serial, reading taken at the tap, instrument display value, and signature of the technician. For lubricant confirmation, an example acceptable record will state the lubricant part number used, the visible condition of the lubrication points, and the batch or lot code from inventory.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration checklist with instrument identifiers and serial numbers.  
- Dust collector differential verification record including the calibrated gauge reading and transducer output, and explicit notation of the alarm threshold "2025 Pa".  
- Lubrication confirmation record citing lubricant part number "CFW-LUB-278" and batch code.  
- Photographs of suspect conditions and HMI screenshots for alarm tests.  
- Electronic entry or scanned logbook page uploaded to the equipment record in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-05.

Acceptance criteria
- Instrument readings are consistent between calibration gauge and equipment transducer, and recorded values are within the documented operating envelope. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is confirmed to actuate at 2025 Pa.  
- Media feed detector responds to simulated conditions and PLC/HMI reflect correct status and interlocks.  
- Lubrication points are serviced using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-278 and inventory batch is recorded. No evidence of abnormal wear or binding is observed that would require immediate mechanical repair.  
- All results are logged and signed, and any nonconformance is entered into the corrective action system with references to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05.

When acceptance criteria are not met, initiate corrective action per SOP-P3-L1-04 and document interim protective measures. Close out actions are recorded per SOP-P3-L1-05 and require supervisor verification before returning the equipment to production.
